To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

there is a consensus among the respondents that the concepts of: (1) family-centered care; (2) health maintenance/promotion; (3) community; (4) levels of prevention; (5) holism; (6) continuity of care; (7) epidemiology; (8) self-care; (9) population-based care; and (10) home health care constitute a theoretical base for public health nursing education.
there is agreement on the essential concepts of public health nursing and that these concepts are consistent with the Consensus Conference recommendations.
public health nursing educators agree that 11 concepts constitute the theoretical base and 8 concepts constitute the practice base for the education of baccalaureates in public health nursing.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an acceptable paradigm for baccalaurate public health nursing.
the development of an ideal public health nursing education paradigm and the identification of the essential knowledge base for the baccalaureately prepared public health nurse.
the development of an ideal curriculum based on an accepted public health nursing paradigm.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

baccalaureates in public health nursing should be prepared as generalists who have the knowledge, skills, and attitudes necessary to provide family-centered, community-based care in a variety of settings.

public health nursing education is a synthesis of the concepts of family centered care, health maintenance/ promotion, community, levels and types of prevention, holistic care, continuity of care across the life cycle, epidemiology, population-based care including home health care, self-care, and health policy and advocacy.

the essential knowledge base for the public health nurse is a synthesis of the concepts of family centered care, health promotion, community, levels and types of prevention, holistic nursing, continuity of care and self-care.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the curriculum of public health nursing should include the concepts of family centered care, health maintenance, community, levels prevention, holistic nursing, continuity of care and epidemiology.

the public health nurse is prepared as a generalist, who is knowledgeable about the concepts of family health, health maintenance and promotion, community, levels and types of prevention, holisim, continuity of care and self-care and who is able to provide care to individuals, families and populations across the life span and in various settings.
there is a paradigm of baccalaurete public health nursing education, and that the paradigm has been defined and is being used by public health nursing educators.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the public health nursing community is in agreement on the essential concepts in baccalaurete public health nursing education, but there is still much work to be done to develop the knowledge base for the profession.
there is a great deal of agreement among educators about the essential concepts in public health nursing education.

the public health nursing education community has a clear idea of what should be taught in public health nursing programs and is willing to work together to ensure that the profession's future practitioners are well prepared to meet the challenges of the 21st century.
